references.text: Sarai says to Abram that Hagar is in her hand, and he can do with her as he sees fit—the same expression about being in someone's hand and doing what seems good.
The Israelites say they are in the Lord's hand, and He can do with them as He sees fit and right—almost identical wording.
Saul is in David's hand, and David can do with him as he sees fit—the same theme of surrendering to another's mercy.
The Ammonites and Syrians say that the Lord will do what is good in His eyes—a similar surrender to another's will.
The man in Gibeah offers his guests and says they may do with them what is good in their eyes—the same expression.
Jeremiah says he is in the people's hands, and they can do with him as they see fit and right—a direct parallel to the words of the Gibeonites.
